summary: Anthropic published details on the safety classifiers used with its redeployed Claude Fable 5 model and proposed an early-draft framework for grading the severity of AI cyber jailbreaks.

practices.reason: The proposed Cyber Jailbreak Severity (CJS) scale gives a concrete, multi-axis scoring rubric a team could apply to grade jailbreak risk in their own systems, though it is explicitly an early draft awaiting feedback.
practices.quote: these factors combine into a banded rating on what we’re calling our Cyber Jailbreak Severity (CJS) scale: None (or “Informational”; CJS-0), Low (CJS-1), Medium (CJS-2), High (CJS-3), and Critical (CJS-4).

practices.reason: Anthropic describes a four-tier taxonomy for classifying dual-use cybersecurity requests, but the specific classifiers and safety-margin tuning are internal to Fable 5 and not directly transferable to another team's stack.
practices.quote: we train our safety classifiers to discern between four categories of cybersecurity use, from the most clearly potentially dangerous to the most clearly potentially benign.
